title: Olive all'ascolana
intro: Green olives stuffed with meat, breaded and fried, the pride of the Marche.

steps.t: Finely chop the carrot and onion and soften them in the olive oil over medium heat for 5 minutes.
steps.label: Base

steps.t: Add the beef, pork and chicken in small pieces and brown for 8 minutes, until no longer pink.
steps.label: Meat

steps.t: Deglaze with the wine and cook over low heat for 10 minutes, until dry and the chicken is cooked through.
steps.label: Simmer

steps.t: Let it cool for 15 minutes, then grind the meat very finely in a food processor.
steps.label: Cool

steps.t: Mix in the Parmesan, 1 egg, nutmeg and salt to make a firm, compact filling.
Stuff each olive with a little filling and press it closed with your fingers, reshaping it.
Roll the olives in flour, then in the 2 beaten eggs, then in breadcrumbs.
Heat the oil to 170 °C and fry the olives in small batches for 3 minutes, until golden.
steps.label: Fry

airfryer.t: Spray the olives lightly with oil and air-fry at 190 °C for 10 minutes, shaking halfway.

steps.t: Drain on paper towels and serve hot, with lemon wedges if you like.

tips.t: Chill the breaded olives for 20 minutes before frying so they hold together in the oil.
Freeze them breaded and fry straight from frozen, adding 1 minute.

title: Gougères
intro: Light, crisp cheese puffs: the classic Burgundy aperitif bite.

steps.t: Heat the oven to 200 °C (conventional) and line two baking sheets with parchment.
Bring the water, butter and salt to a boil until the butter has melted.
Take off the heat, add the flour all at once and stir; return to the heat for 2 minutes until the dough pulls away from the pan.
steps.label: Dough

steps.t: Transfer the dough to a bowl and let it cool for 5 minutes.
steps.label: Cool

steps.t: Beat in the eggs one at a time until the dough is smooth and glossy.
Stir in 100 g of the Gruyère and plenty of black pepper.
Pipe walnut-sized balls, well spaced, and sprinkle with the remaining cheese.
Bake for 25 minutes without opening the oven, until puffed and golden. Serve warm.
steps.label: Bake

tips.t: Prick each one on the side as it comes out of the oven to let steam escape and keep them crisp.
A pinch of nutmeg or smoked paprika in the dough adds depth.
Serve with a well-chilled Chablis or Crémant de Bourgogne.

title: Pork gyoza
intro: Japanese dumplings, crisp underneath and tender on top, with soy-vinegar dip.

steps.t: Finely chop the cabbage, salt it and let it sit for 10 minutes, then squeeze it dry.
steps.label: Cabbage

steps.t: Mix the pork, cabbage, chopped scallions, grated garlic and ginger, 1 tbsp soy sauce and the sesame oil.
Put a teaspoon of filling on each wrapper, wet the edge, fold into a half-moon and pleat it shut.
Heat the oil in a nonstick pan with a lid and fry the gyoza flat side down for 2 minutes.
steps.label: Fry

steps.t: Pour in the water, cover and steam for 5 minutes, until the water is gone and the pork is cooked through.
steps.label: Steam

steps.t: Uncover and cook 1 more minute, until the bottoms are golden and crisp.
steps.label: Crisp

steps.t: Mix the remaining soy sauce with the rice vinegar and a few drops of chili oil, and serve.

tips.t: Stir 1 tsp flour into the steaming water for a lacy, crisp skirt joining the gyoza.
Freeze them raw on a tray, then bag them; cook from frozen with 2 extra minutes of steam.

title: Tuscan chicken liver crostini
intro: Chicken liver pâté with capers and anchovies on toast, a Tuscan feast starter.

ing.n: vin santo or dry white wine

steps.t: Trim the livers, removing sinew and any green bits, then cut into pieces.
Gently soften the chopped onion in the oil with the sage over low heat for 8 minutes.
steps.label: Onion

steps.t: Add the livers and brown them over high heat for 5 minutes.
steps.label: Livers

steps.t: Deglaze with the vin santo, add the stock (store-bought is fine) and simmer 15 minutes, until the livers are cooked through.
steps.label: Simmer

steps.t: Add the capers and anchovies and chop everything by knife or in a processor to a rustic paste. Season.
Toast the bread slices in the oven at 200 °C for 5 minutes, until crisp.
steps.label: Toast

steps.t: Spread the warm pâté on the toasts and serve straight away.

tips.t: Do as the Tuscans do: dip the edge of each toast briefly in hot stock before spreading.
Serve with a glass of young Chianti or vin santo.

title: Onion bhaji
intro: Crisp, spiced Indian onion fritters made with chickpea flour.

steps.t: Thinly slice the onions, toss with the salt and let them sit for 10 minutes to release their juices.
steps.label: Onions

steps.t: Add both flours, the spices, and the chopped green chili and cilantro, and mix with your hands.
Add the water a little at a time until a thick batter coats the onions.
Heat the oil in a deep pan to 170 °C.

airfryer.t: Heat the air fryer to 190 °C and brush the basket with a little oil.

steps.t: Drop in small heaps of the mixture and fry for 4 minutes, turning, until deep golden and crisp.
steps.label: Fry

airfryer.t: Place flattened heaps in the basket, brush with oil and air-fry 10 minutes at 190 °C, turning halfway.

steps.t: Drain on paper towels and serve hot with mint or tamarind chutney.

tips.t: If you are not keeping it vegan, dip them in tzatziki or a yogurt raita.
Add 1 tsp fennel seeds or garam masala to the batter.

title: Bacon-wrapped dates
intro: The sweet-and-salty Spanish tapa: almond-stuffed dates in crisp bacon.

steps.t: Heat the oven to 200 °C and line a baking sheet with parchment.
Slit the dates lengthwise, remove the pits and push an almond into each.
Cut the bacon slices in half, wrap one around each date and secure with a toothpick.
Bake for 12 minutes, turning halfway, until the bacon is golden and crisp.
steps.label: Bake

airfryer.t: Air-fry at 190 °C for 8 minutes, turning halfway, until the bacon is crisp.

steps.t: Let them rest for 3 minutes, as the filling is very hot, then serve warm.
steps.label: Rest

tips.t: Swap the almond for a cube of blue cheese or Manchego.
Serve with pimientos de Padrón for a round of tapas.

title: Causa limeña, layered potato terrine
intro: Lime and chili potato layered with tuna mayo and avocado, served cold.

steps.t: Boil the whole potatoes in their skins in salted water until tender but not falling apart.
steps.label: Potatoes

steps.t: Meanwhile hard-boil the eggs: 9 minutes in boiling water, then into cold water.
steps.label: Eggs

steps.t: Mix the tuna with the very finely chopped onion, the mayonnaise (store-bought is fine), salt and pepper.
Blend the seeded chili with the oil and turmeric until smooth and yellow.
Peel the potatoes while still hot, press them through a ricer and let the mash cool.
steps.label: Cool

steps.t: Knead the mash by hand with the lime juice, chili oil and salt: it should be smooth, tangy and spicy.
In a film-lined mold, spread half the mash, then salted avocado slices, the tuna and the remaining mash.
Press lightly, cover and chill for at least 1 hour so it sets.
steps.label: Chill

steps.t: Unmold, cut into portions with a wet knife and top with egg wedges and olives.

tips.t: Use 2 tbsp ají amarillo paste instead of the chili and turmeric for Lima's deep yellow.
For causa de pollo, use 300 g poached, shredded chicken breast instead of tuna.
Use a ricer and your hands: a blender turns the potato gluey.

title: Anticuchos, spicy beef skewers
intro: Beef skewers marinated in vinegar, garlic and paprika, grilled as on Lima's streets.

steps.t: Soak the skewers in water. Cut the beef into 4 x 3 cm pieces, 1 cm thick.
Crush the garlic with a pinch of salt, then mix with the paprikas, chili, cumin, oregano, vinegar, 2 tbsp oil and pepper.
Rub the marinade into the beef, cover and leave in the fridge for at least 2 hours.
steps.label: Marinate

steps.t: Boil the potatoes in their skins in salted water until tender.
steps.label: Potatoes

steps.t: Meanwhile thread 3 or 4 pieces of beef tightly onto each skewer. Mix the leftover marinade with the remaining oil.
Heat the grill pan until very hot and cook the skewers 2-3 minutes per side, brushing with the marinade, until charred.
steps.label: Grill

bbq.t: Cook over glowing coals, close to the heat, 2-3 minutes per side, brushing with the marinade.

steps.t: Peel the potatoes, slice them thickly and brown them on the grill with a little marinade.
steps.label: Potatoes

steps.t: Serve the anticuchos piping hot, still on their skewers, on top of the potatoes.

tips.t: Real anticuchos are beef heart: ask your butcher for one, trimmed of sinew.
Use 3 tbsp ají panca paste from a Latin shop instead of the paprikas for a fruitier, smoky taste.
Serve with huancaína sauce and a boiled corn cob.

title: Gỏi cuốn, fresh spring rolls
intro: Prawns, pork and fresh herbs wrapped in rice paper, with a thick peanut dipping sauce.

steps.t: Simmer the pork belly in salted water for 25 minutes, until cooked through. Let it cool, then slice thinly.
steps.label: Pork

steps.t: Meanwhile boil the prawns for 2 minutes, until pink and curled. Peel them and halve lengthwise.
steps.label: Prawns

steps.t: Cook the rice vermicelli for 4 minutes (or as the pack says), rinse under cold water and drain well.
steps.label: Vermicelli

steps.t: Cut the cucumber into sticks, wash and dry the lettuce and herbs. Line everything up on the counter.
Sauce: fry the minced garlic in the oil for 30 seconds, add hoisin, peanut butter and water and simmer 2 minutes, until smooth.
steps.label: Sauce

steps.t: Dip a rice paper sheet in warm water for 2 or 3 seconds and lay it on a damp board: it softens as you fill it.
On the lower third lay lettuce, a little vermicelli, cucumber, pork and herbs; put 3 prawn halves in the middle, red side down.
Fold in the sides and roll up tightly, tucking in a chive stalk so it sticks out of one end. Repeat with the other sheets.
Serve right away with the sauce in small bowls, topped with chopped peanuts and sliced chili.

tips.t: Only wet the rice paper for a few seconds: it finishes softening on the board, while a soggy one tears.
Serve nước chấm: 3 tbsp fish sauce, 3 sugar, 3 lime juice, 9 water, plus minced garlic and chili.
Make them up to 2 hours ahead and cover with a damp towel. In the fridge the rice paper turns hard.

title: Cheese briouats
intro: Crisp pastry triangles filled with cheese and fresh herbs.

steps.t: Mash the feta and ricotta with a fork, then mix in the beaten egg, chopped parsley and cilantro and some black pepper.
Cut each filo sheet into 4 strips about 8 cm wide and keep them covered with a damp towel.
Brush a strip with butter, put a teaspoon of filling at one end and fold into triangles to the end. Seal with butter.
Fry the briouats in oil at 170 °C, a few at a time, until golden; drain on paper towels.
steps.label: Cook

oven.t: Brush with butter and bake at 200 °C for 15 minutes, turning halfway, until golden.

airfryer.t: Brush with butter and air-fry at 180 °C for 8 minutes, until golden.

steps.t: Serve hot or warm, alongside the cooked salads.

tips.t: Meat version: 300 g ground beef cooked with onion, cumin, cinnamon and parsley, bound with 1 egg.
Always keep the filo under a damp towel: in the open air it dries out in minutes and cracks.
With warqa from Moroccan shops instead of filo they're even thinner and crisper.

title: Haemul pajeon, seafood scallion pancake
intro: A crisp Korean pancake packed with spring onions, prawns and squid, with a soy dip.

steps.t: Mix the soy, vinegar, gochugaru and sesame: that's the dipping sauce.
Cut the spring onions into 10 cm lengths, halving thick white parts. Roughly chop the prawns and squid; slice the chilli.
Whisk the flours, salt, egg and ice-cold water into a runny batter; a few strokes are enough, a few lumps are fine.
Heat 2 tbsp oil in a 26 cm pan, lay in half the spring onions, pour over half the batter and scatter with half the seafood and chilli.
Cook over medium-high heat, pressing with a spatula, until the underside is golden and crisp.
steps.label: First side

steps.t: Flip it, add 1 tbsp oil around the edge and cook until the seafood is cooked and the crust is crisp.
steps.label: Second side

steps.t: Repeat with the rest. Cut into squares and serve straight away with the dipping sauce.

tips.t: Ice-cold water and a barely mixed batter are the secret to a crisp, not chewy, pajeon.
In Korea it's eaten on rainy days with a bowl of makgeolli, the cloudy rice wine.
Use Korean buchim-garu pancake mix instead of the two flours for a ready-seasoned batter.

title: Mercimek köftesi, lentil bulgur bites
intro: Cold red lentil and bulgur bites, wrapped in lettuce with a squeeze of lemon.

steps.t: Rinse the lentils and cook them in the 500 ml water over low heat for 18 minutes, until mushy and the water is absorbed.
steps.label: Lentils

steps.t: Turn off the heat, stir in the bulgur, cover and leave for 15 minutes: the heat makes the bulgur swell.
steps.label: Bulgur

steps.t: Meanwhile chop the onion and fry it in the oil for 6 minutes until golden. Add tomato paste, chilli and cumin and cook 1 minute.
steps.label: Onion

steps.t: Tip the onion mixture onto the lentils and knead by hand while still warm for 3 to 4 minutes, until it holds its shape.
Let it cool, then add the chopped spring onions and parsley, the juice of half the lemon and salt, and knead again.
With damp hands, take a walnut-sized piece and squeeze it in your fist: the finger marks should stay.
Serve cold on lettuce leaves with wedges of the remaining lemon: wrap each one in a leaf to eat.

tips.t: If the mix is too soft, add a spoonful of bulgur and wait another 10 minutes.
A drizzle of pomegranate molasses (nar ekşisi) makes them sweet-sour, Istanbul style.
Covered in the fridge they keep 2 days and taste even better the next day.

title: Potato and pea samosas
intro: Crisp pastry triangles filled with spiced potato and peas, India's favourite street snack.

steps.t: Mix the flour, 1 tsp salt and 3 tbsp oil, rubbing with your fingertips until it holds together when squeezed.
Add the water little by little and knead for 3 minutes into a firm dough; cover and let it rest.
steps.label: Rest

steps.t: Meanwhile boil the whole potatoes in salted water until tender; peel and crumble them roughly.
steps.label: Potatoes

steps.t: Heat the remaining oil in a pan, let the cumin and coriander sizzle, then add ginger, chopped chilies and peas.
steps.label: Peas

steps.t: Add the potatoes, garam masala, chili, lemon juice, salt and cilantro; mix and let it cool completely.
steps.label: Cool

steps.t: Divide the dough into 6 balls, roll each into a thin 18 cm oval and cut it in half.
Shape each half into a cone, sealing the straight edge with water, fill with 2 tbsp filling and press it shut.
Heat the oil to just 150 °C and fry the samosas over low heat, turning, until golden and crisp.
steps.label: Fry

airfryer.t: Brush the samosas with oil and air-fry at 180 °C for 14 minutes, turning halfway.

oven.t: Brush with oil and bake on a lined tray at 200 °C for 25 minutes, turning halfway.

steps.t: Drain on paper towels and serve warm with mint or tamarind chutney.

tips.t: Keep the oil at 150 °C, no hotter: the pastry blisters into tiny bubbles and stays crisp, not greasy.
For a street-stall flavour, add ½ tsp ajwain to the dough and use amchur instead of lemon.
Freeze them uncooked on a tray and fry from frozen, adding 3 minutes.
